note 4 overlapping conductor shape(s) were merged into 2 — copper that overlaps on one level is one conductor, in 3D as in the planar model.
note Port 1 ('1') at (0, 0 µm) was taken to be on the conductor's low-x (left) end (inferred from the nearest conductor boundary) of level 0 ('M1'), driving current in the +x direction, at 50 Ω.
note Port 2 ('2') at (2300, 0 µm) was taken to be on the conductor's high-x (right) end (inferred from the nearest conductor boundary) of level 1 ('M2'), driving current in the −x direction, at 50 Ω.
note Port 1 at its line's end is a wave port returning through 'Ground' (the air box's floor), below the line: as this setup names.
note Port 2 at its line's end is a wave port returning through 'Ground' (the air box's floor), below the line: as this setup names.
note Port 1 is a wave port on the air box's xmin face: 2000 × 800 µm (10 line widths × 8 heights, the sizing rule's), its reference plane on the face.
note Port 2's wave-port region is clipped to the air box's xmax face; the box is smaller than the sizing rule asks for there.
note Port 2 is a wave port on the air box's xmax face: 2100 × 1205 µm (15.25 line widths × 8 heights, the sizing rule's), its reference plane on the face.
note 2 conductor piece(s) are sheets because this setup states Conductors: Sheets, the planar model's own idealisation: each carries its conductivity and thickness rather than a meshed volume.
note 'M1', 'M2', 'Via' name no material, so their σ is a number of unknown temperature and is used as given at 20 °C. Name a material with an α₂₀ to have it evaluated at the operating temperature.
note The air box's floor is 'Ground' as a PEC plane at 5 µm: it is the lowest ground-reference conductor, nothing is drawn on it and nothing is drawn below it. The AirBox ZMin padding does not apply to a floor on the plane.
